claim_verdicts.evidence: Definitional: the lesson's definition matches glossary.yaml short_en for observability ('How well you can tell what happened inside a running system from the data it sends out'). No docs root in versions.yaml defines the term; the monitoring contrast is framing, not version-dependent behaviour. The book in source_hint is not an allowed source and was not consulted.

stage-2 docker-compose.yml api env: Logging__Console__FormatterName: "json"; Program.cs:99 app.UseHttpMetrics(), :118 app.MapMetrics(); Directory.Packages.props at stage-2 has prometheus-net.AspNetCore 8.2.1 and no OpenTelemetry package.
donhang-api.json at stage-2: panel "title": "5xx responses per second", "expr": "sum(rate(http_requests_received_total{code=~\"5..\"}[5m]))" — a summed rate with no per-order label.

Docs: "The order you add middleware components in the Program.cs file defines the order in which the middleware components are invoked on requests and the reverse order for the response." Program.cs:106-107 registers RequestLoggingMiddleware then ExceptionHandlingMiddleware; RequestLoggingMiddleware logs after `await next(context)`, ExceptionHandlingMiddleware logs inside its catch.

Captured run: {"EventId":0,"LogLevel":"Information","Category":"DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware","Message":"GET /api/v1/products/2 responded 200 in ...ms","State":{"Method":"GET","Path":"/api/v1/products/2","StatusCode":200,"ElapsedMs":...,"{OriginalFormat}":"..."}}. Round 3: section 5 now says placeholders sit under the line's State object, matching this output.

Execution: the captured request line (written inside the ASP.NET Core request, where hosting opens a scope) has no Scopes key — only EventId, LogLevel, Category, Message, State. Compose sets only Logging__Console__FormatterName; appsettings.json sets no IncludeScopes. The default value itself was not found as a sentence in refs/dotnet-docs (overview.md:141 only says IncludeScopes indicates whether scopes are enabled).

Round 3: claim unchanged; section 5 now says only 'Its exception text describes the failure' (stack-trace sentence removed). Code part verified: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:61-64 `catch (Exception ex) { logger.LogError(ex, "unhandled exception"); ... Status500InternalServerError ... }`. Still not verified that the JSON line carries the exception text: no match in refs/dotnet-docs console files; no exception line in outputs; lab not run.

Captured run: "== POST /api/v1/orders for a product that does not exist\n  -> 500" then {"LogLevel":"Information","Category":"DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware","Message":"POST /api/v1/orders responded 500 in ...ms"}. OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync does no product lookup; FK 23503 is not the UniqueViolation filter, so it reaches catch (Exception).

issues.text: q1 option a (reworded in round 2) is the key but claims more than the panel can show. The 5xx panel is sum(rate(http_requests_received_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) over every endpoint, and the q1 explanation itself says it shows 'how often requests failed, never which ones'. It cannot say that checkouts specifically were failing; the key is defensible only as least wrong.
